hook: Clement Delangue co-founded Hugging Face in 2016 with Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf, originally as a chatbot app, and steered it into the default home for sharing open-source AI models and datasets. Before that he worked in product management at Moodstocks, a computer vision startup that Google acquired the same year Hugging Face began. As CEO he built a platform that by September 2026 hosted more than 3 million models and 500,000 datasets used by more than 18 million developers. That same month he agreed to sell the company to Nvidia for roughly 12.9 billion dollars, negotiating to keep Hugging Face open across clouds, frameworks and chip vendors rather than tied to Nvidia's hardware alone.
name: Clement Delangue

quote.text: But for it to happen at a larger scale, it needs more compute, more support, more collaboration, and more visibility. That's why we went to talk to Jensen, who offered to do exactly that with us.

standing.standing: Clement Delangue is co-founder and CEO of Hugging Face. He co-founded Hugging Face in 2016 with Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf. The company began as a chatbot app and became the default home for sharing open-source AI models and datasets. By September 2026 the platform hosted more than 3 million models, 500,000 datasets and 1 million applications used by more than 18 million developers. That same month he agreed to sell the company to Nvidia for roughly 12.9 billion dollars, with the announcement on September 3, 2026. He negotiated to keep Hugging Face open across clouds, frameworks and chip vendors rather than tied to Nvidia's hardware alone.
